items.text: The interesting thing about AI agents is that as a theoretical matter, their inference can kind of run anywhere. AI is one of the few areas of technology that isn’t *as* sensitive to latency back to the user. Long running agents are now going to be the norm, which means it’s ok to send off work to an AI factory somewhere and that work can essentially be largely done within that remote data center and a final result spit back to the user. The data can pass into these systems in an encrypted manner, be combed through by agents, and then disregarded right after. items.text: If building datacenters becomes harder, it is obvious that you should be super long anyone who has existing capacity (aka hyperscalers). It's not like the demand for the spice is going way -- it is only continuing to go up. Thus the spice holders will win big. What will suffer is the rate of new model training. I guess we will pace the frontier after all. The body politic speaketh.
